topics.name: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at, between)

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct past tense.
options: Dhyan Chand scored two goals in the final.
Dhyan Chand scoring two goals in the final.
Dhyan Chand score two goals in the final.
questions.rule: The action is over, so use the simple past: scored.

options: The ground were wet after the rain.
The ground was wet after the rain.
The ground am wet after the rain.
questions.rule: One thing (the ground) in the past takes was.

options: Hockey is played with an stick and a ball.
Hockey is played with a stick and a ball.
Hockey is played with a stick and an ball.
questions.rule: stick and ball begin with consonant sounds, so both take a.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: buys
bought
buying

questions.rule: Buy is irregular. Its past form is bought, not buyed.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: is
were
be

questions.rule: Both teams is plural, so use were.

options: on
in
at
questions.rule: Use at with a clock time: at 11 am, at noon.

options: an
many
a
questions.rule: soldier begins with a consonant sound, so use a.
Subject + past verb + object: India won the gold medal.
Subject + was + describing words: The field was very wet.

chat: Did you watch the hockey match yesterday?
options: Yes, I watched it on TV.
Yes, I watch it on TV.
Yes, I watching it on TV.
questions.rule: The question is about yesterday, so answer in the simple past: watched.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct past tense.
options: The German ruler left the stadium early.
The German ruler leaved the stadium early.
The German ruler leaving the stadium early.
questions.rule: Leave is irregular: leave - left.

options: Dhyan Chand was born in 29 August.
Dhyan Chand was born at 29 August.
Dhyan Chand was born on 29 August.
questions.rule: Use on with dates and days: on 29 August, on Monday.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: on
at
by

questions.rule: A date takes on: on 29 August.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: these
much
a

questions.rule: strong begins with a consonant sound, so use a, not an.

options: were
was
is
questions.rule: People is plural, so use were in the past.

questions.after: off his shoes and ran barefoot.
options: takes
took
taken
questions.rule: ran shows the past, so use the past form too: take - took.
Use in with cities and countries: in Berlin, in India.
an before a vowel sound (an orange), a before a consonant sound (a sandwich).

options: I was at the doctor's clinic.
I were at the doctor's clinic.
I am at the doctor's clinic yesterday.
questions.rule: I takes was in the past, not were.

chat: What did you buy at the sports shop?
options: I bought a new pair of shoes.
I buyed a new pair of shoes.
I buy a new pair of shoes yesterday.
questions.rule: Did you buy asks about the past. Answer with the past form: bought.

options: The Indian team didn't lost the final.
The Indian team not lose the final.
The Indian team didn't lose the final.
questions.rule: After didn't, use the base form of the verb: didn't lose.

options: The Indians weren't comfortable on the wet ground.
The Indians wasn't comfortable on the wet ground.
The Indians not were comfortable on the wet ground.
questions.rule: The Indians is plural, so use weren't (were not).

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct prepositions.
options: The match was played at the morning on 15 August.
The match was played in the morning on 15 August.
The match was played on the morning in 15 August.
questions.rule: Say in the morning, but on a date.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: hurts
hurting
hurt

questions.rule: Hurt does not change in the past: hurt - hurt. It matches pounced.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: is
were
has

questions.rule: Two sticks is plural, so say There were.

options: a
an
many
questions.rule: The h in honest is silent, so it begins with a vowel sound: an honest game.

options: on
in
at
questions.rule: Use at with exact times: at noon, at 11 am.
In a question, were comes before the subject: Were the players nervous?

options: It is in 29 August.
It is at 29 August.
It is on 29 August.
questions.rule: Dates take on: on 29 August.

chat: What did you get for your birthday?
options: I got a umbrella and a hockey stick.
I got an umbrella and an hockey stick.
I got an umbrella and a hockey stick.
questions.rule: an umbrella (vowel sound), a hockey stick (consonant sound).

options: The children cheered when India scored.
The childs cheered when India scored.
The children cheer when India scored.
questions.rule: The plural of child is children, and both verbs stay in the past: cheered, scored.

options: He and his team were proud of the win.
Him and his team were proud of the win.
He and his team was proud of the win.
questions.rule: The subject is He (not him). He and his team are more than one, so use were.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: most
very
much

questions.rule: faster already means 'more fast'. Never say more faster. Say much faster.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: few
a
many

questions.rule: The h in hockey is sounded, so it takes a.

options: were
was
is
questions.rule: These shoes is plural and yesterday is past, so use were.

questions.after: the first goal in the final?
options: score
scoring
scored
questions.rule: When Who is the subject, use the past verb directly: Who scored?
Wh- word + did + subject + base verb: Why did he run?
Use on with a day, even with a part of it: on Sunday morning.

chat: Who is taller, you or your brother?
options: My brother is more tall than me.
My brother is tallest than me.
My brother is taller than me.
questions.rule: To compare two people, add -er to short adjectives: tall - taller than.

chat: Why did you come home late from practice?
options: The bus was late, so I walked home.
The bus were late, so I walked home.
The bus was late, so I walk home.
questions.rule: One bus takes was, and both parts stay in the past: was, walked.

options: Although the German players tried their level best, they could not stopped India.
Although the German players tried their level best, they could not stop India.
Although the German players try their level best, they could not stop India.
questions.rule: Keep both parts in the past (tried), and use the base form after could not: stop.

options: Dhyan Chand practised in night in the moonlight because he was busy during the day.
Dhyan Chand practised at night in the moonlight because he was busy during the day.
Dhyan Chand practised at night in a moonlight because he was busy during the day.
questions.rule: We say at night and in the moonlight.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: much
most
many

questions.rule: the ... in the team compares one with all the others, so use the most famous.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: refuses
refusing
refused

questions.rule: offered is past, so the second action is past too: refused.

questions.after: ready long before the match began.
options: were
was
is
questions.rule: Two subjects joined by and are plural, so use were.

questions.after: the two German defenders and into the goal.
options: among
on
between
questions.rule: Use between for two people or things; among is for more than two.
The German players is plural, so it takes were.

chat: What did your team do after you won the match?
options: We celebrated with ice cream and went home.
We celebrated with ice cream and go home.
We celebrate with ice cream and went home.
questions.rule: Both actions happened in the past, so both verbs are past: celebrated, went.

chat: Where is the hockey match today?
options: It's at the stadium near an old temple.
It's at the stadium near a old temple.
It's at stadium near an old temple.
questions.rule: Say the stadium (a particular one) and an old temple (vowel sound).

chat: Were you and Sahil at the match yesterday?
options: Yes, we was. It was a thrilling game!
Yes, we were. It were a thrilling game!
Yes, we were. It was a thrilling game!
questions.rule: We takes were; it takes was.
